en.title: Counting Strings Without k Consecutive Identical Letters
en.description:
Count the lowercase English strings of length n that do not contain k or more consecutive identical letters, modulo 1000000007. At most k−1 identical letters may appear consecutively; do not misread this as allowing k.

The ranges added by this site for missing bounds and the recovery of source typos are described in the input protocol.
en.input: The input gives n k. Full original bounds: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤k<n, so a valid n is in fact ≥2; do not change this to k≤n or change the forbidden length to k+1.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 16250; 0; 11880050. They have been checked by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Let F[i] be the number of valid strings of length i. For i<k it is 26^i; F[k]=26^k−26; for i>k, F[i]=26F[i−1]−25F[i−k]. When k=1, output 0 directly.
